area: Area 1: architectures that combine graphs and embeddings
current_formulation: Passage nodes join an LLM-extracted graph, and embedding similarity seeds a Personalized PageRank walk over it.

steps.formulation: Vector RAG: a generator reads text chunks retrieved from a dense vector index; the index is replaced as a whole to update knowledge.
steps.quote: the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia

criticism.quote: RAG fails on global questions directed at an entire text corpus

steps.formulation: GraphRAG: an LLM extracts an entity graph, communities of the graph are summarised in advance, and the summaries answer global questions.
steps.quote: to pregenerate community summaries for all groups of closely related entities

criticism.quote: GraphRAG must dismantle its existing community structure to incorporate new entities and relationships, followed by complete regeneration

steps.formulation: LightRAG: short keys of entities and relations sit in a vector database; a vector match is followed by a one-hop graph expansion, and new documents are added by set union.
steps.quote: The algorithm uses an efficient vector database to match local query keywords with candidate entities

criticism.quote: their performance on more basic factual memory tasks drops considerably below standard RAG

steps.formulation: LazyGraphRAG: the GraphRAG authors drop up-front summarisation and use text chunk embeddings to rank communities of a noun-phrase graph at query time.
steps.quote: Uses text chunk embeddings and chunk-community relationships to first rank text chunks by similarity to the query

steps.formulation: HippoRAG 2: passage nodes join the graph, and passage embedding similarity sets the reset probabilities of the PageRank walk.
steps.quote: passage nodes receive scores proportional to their embedding similarity

criticism.quote: GraphRAG frequently underperforms vanilla RAG on many real-world tasks
